prereg.question: r2017 put the churn on the veto edge (84.2%) and concluded the fix must damp the score, not the membership. Does smoothing the residual rank over K rebalance dates buy that churn back, and what does it cost?

arms.K=1: book rebuilt with the residual rank averaged over the last 1 rebalance dates, re-ranked, same 80/20 split
arms.K=2: book rebuilt with the residual rank averaged over the last 2 rebalance dates, re-ranked, same 80/20 split
arms.K=3: book rebuilt with the residual rank averaged over the last 3 rebalance dates, re-ranked, same 80/20 split
arms.K=4: book rebuilt with the residual rank averaged over the last 4 rebalance dates, re-ranked, same 80/20 split

prereg.decomposition: net_K - net_1 = (gross_K - gross_1) + 2c*(turn_1 - turn_K), computed, not fitted
prereg.verdict: SMOOTHING_PAYS / SMOOTHING_COSTS require |paired t| >= 2; everything else is SMOOTHING_NOT_SEPARABLE

spec.smoothing: mean of the cross-sectional ranks over the last K dates the name was eligible, then re-ranked and split at the parent's 80/20 line
spec.why_ranks: the residual is a per-period regression error; its dispersion moves, so a raw average would be dominated by the noisiest dates
spec.why_rerank: keeps every arm at exactly 80% of eligible names, so the difference is which names, never how many
